PullRequest.Title: sessions: rename the session from the main chat tab's Rename
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #342608

## What changed

In the Agents window, when a session shows chat tabs (a main chat plus a side chat or nested session), the **main chat tab's** context menu offered **Rename...** whenever the chat itself could be renamed. Picking it ran the chat-rename command, which deliberately refuses a session's main chat because its title is the session title, so nothing happened.

Now, in `ChatCompositeBar`:

- **Main chat tab:** Rename runs the session rename (`RENAME_SESSION_COMMAND_ID`). This matches F2 on that tab and Rename on the session in the Sessions list. The item is offered only when the session supports renaming (`supportsRename`).
- **Side-chat tabs:** unchanged. They keep the inline chat rename (`RENAME_CHAT_COMMAND_ID` with `inline: true`), gated on the chat's `canRename`.

The regression came from #336931 (1.139). It routed the tab's Rename through the shared chat-rename command and excluded the main chat there, but didn't update the menu's condition.

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, open a session and add a side chat (the **+** next to the session in the list), so the session shows chat tabs.
2. Right-click the **main** chat tab and choose **Rename...**. Expect a "New agent session title" prompt; the new title renames the session.
3. Right-click the **side chat** tab and choose **Rename...**. Expect the tab title to switch to inline editing, as before.

## Validation

Validated on top of `origin/main` at `85379af45f0`.

- Red first: the two new tests failed before the fix (main tab ran `sessions.chatCompositeBar.renameChat`; main tab offered Rename when the session couldn't be renamed). The existing side-chat test passed.
- `npm run transpile-client` → passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/chatCompositeBar.test.ts` → 41 passing
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --runGlob 'vs/sessions/**/browser/**/*.test.js'` → 7031 passing, 22 pending, 0 failing
- `npm run typecheck-client` → passed (0 errors)
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/browser/parts/chatCompositeBar.ts src/vs/sessions/test/browser/chatCompositeBar.test.ts` → passed
- `node build/hygiene.ts src/vs/sessions/browser/parts/chatCompositeBar.ts src/vs/sessions/test/browser/chatCompositeBar.test.ts` → passed (pre-commit hygiene also passed)
- Component fixtures (`chatCompositeBar.fixture.ts`, `sessionHeader.fixture.ts`): not rendered locally because the Component Explorer server isn't available in this environment. The change touches only the right-click menu actions, not the rendered tab DOM, so CI's screenshot check should be unchanged.
- No live Agents-window run. The path is deterministic and covered by the DOM tests above.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **Header inline rename renames the default chat, not the session.** `SessionHeaderBar` commits via `renameChat(session, activeChat.resource)`. For local agent-host sessions, renaming the default chat sets its own title override instead of renaming the session. This is a likely way into the known issue where the default chat's tab keeps its own title after a session rename. Renaming the session from the main tab can surface that existing issue.
- **Possible F2 mis-target:** if the main tab has keyboard focus while a side chat is the group's active chat, `SessionFocusedChatIsRenameTargetContext` (bound to the active chat) is true. F2 then falls back to `getFocusedChat()`, which returns the group's active chat, and prompts to rename the side chat. Found by reading the code; not verified live.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the main chat tab context menu in an Agents session with multiple chat tabs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The context-menu event synchronously reads chat capabilities, provider identity, and the session's supportsRename observable, then constructs a small fixed action list before the menu can render.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected tab and a fixed set of at most four menu action groups; work does not scale with session count, chat history, or tab count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI event; no queued, parallel, or asynchronous work is started by opening the menu.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Only already-materialized session/chat observables and the provider registry are read; there is no cold-cache fetch, cache miss, or changed cache lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed getActions closure and the implementation of getChatCapabilities show the complete synchronous path and no transitive boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Observable/provider-registry lookup duration is not measured, but both are bounded in-memory reads and the diff adds only one observable get.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The added session capability read is O(1), creates no retained state, and does not add layout, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Choose Rename on the main chat tab and confirm a changed session title
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The action invokes the existing rename-session command, waits for user quick input, and after confirmation awaits one sessions-management provider rename before completion. Before the PR, the main-tab action invoked chat rename, which rejected the main chat before showing input or crossing a provider boundary; the new boundary is the intended user-requested operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch one SessionTitleChanged action to the owning agent-host connection; remote cloud-sandbox providers may first await their single task rename handler.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one provider rename per confirmed changed title; no loop or fan-out across chats or sessions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The incorrectly routed main-chat rename command returned after identifying the target as the main chat and issued no provider call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The command awaits provider rename where applicable, so this one operation is on the explicit rename command's completion path, not on menu opening or rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A single session and title string; cost is independent of chat count, session count, and conversation history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One command invocation and at most one provider operation per user confirmation; no Promise.all, burst, retry loop, or cross-key concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider/session lookup uses existing in-memory registries and session caches. Cold versus warm state does not change call cardinality; unsupported/disconnected providers are gated or fail through existing behavior, with no retry or negative-cache loop added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed action directly calls RENAME_SESSION_COMMAND_ID, whose handler performs one sessionsManagementService.renameSession call after confirmation, and the management service forwards once to the provider.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider latency varies by local versus remote session, but it is a one-shot operation initiated by the user and required to persist the rename.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new single boundary call is the requested rename operation, is not multiplied or moved onto a passive UI path, and has bounded cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open Rename on a side-chat tab
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The side-chat branch creates and executes the same inline chat-rename action as before; context-menu capability evaluation and inline editor activation remain unchanged.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected side-chat tab; no work scales with the number of chats or sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI action with unchanged sequencing; no new concurrent work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Reads existing in-memory chat/session observables only; no cache behavior changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the ternary preserves the previous RENAME_CHAT_COMMAND_ID action and arguments for non-main chats.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material for PR causality because the side-chat branch is behaviorally unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The diff only separates the main-chat action; side-chat work, frequency, and lifetime are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced tab creation, context-menu opening, both rename command handlers, sessions management, and local/remote provider persistence. The patch adds one bounded observable read per main-tab context-menu opening and one intended provider operation per confirmed main-session rename, with no scaling fan-out, eager boundary work, retained state, or hot rendering/layout cost.
